DECISION D38 - FROZEN N1D CONTRACT

Challenger
Each accepted novel cluster receives weight 2^(-age_hours/24) at the scheduled 17:30 America/New_York cutoff. The cycle weights are summed and mapped through an issuer-local eight-quarter TRAIN ECDF.

Unchanged authority
Article admissibility, stale-update and novelty rules, issuer identity, future h5 path-volatility outcome, prior-h5 path-volatility control, current/prior-60 dollar-volume control, and next-open alignment remain frozen.

Confirmation
Only 2025Q1 through 2026Q2 are evaluated. Success requires all integrity checks, positive mean recency ordering, positive recency ordering in at least 4/6 quarters, mean lift of at least 0.01, and positive lift in at least 4/6 quarters.

DECISION D38 - FIXED DECAY SEMANTICS

Reading the curve
An article cluster at the cutoff receives weight 1.0; the weight halves every 24 calendar hours. At 72 hours the weight is 0.125.

Why this form
The clock-time decay is simple, monotone, auditable, and fixed before confirmation inspection. It expresses the hypothesis that recently arrived information may remain less resolved.

Boundary
No grid search, TRAIN selection, alternate half-life, market-hours clock, source weighting, sentiment, or text model was evaluated.

DECISION D39 - PRIMARY CONFIRMATION EVIDENCE

Absolute ordering
Recency partial Spearman is positive in 5/6 quarters and averages 0.036938, so the representation still carries modest uncertainty context.

Relative ordering
Equal count averages 0.038762. Recency lift averages -0.001824, not the required +0.01. Lift is positive in only 3/6 quarters, not the required 4/6.

Decision logic
The challenger must beat the simpler accepted measure, not merely remain positive. Both complexity-penalty gates fail.

DECISION D39 - TIE RESOLUTION IS DIAGNOSTIC

Evidence
The recency representation produces substantially more distinct issuer-local TRAIN percentile values in every confirmation quarter than equal count.

Meaning
Recency does what it was mechanically intended to do: it distinguishes cycles with equal article counts but different timing. That additional granularity did not improve conditional future-volatility ordering.

Teaching point
Feature richness, variance, and tie resolution are not substitutes for incremental predictive evidence.

Every one of the 24 issuers contributes admissible novel-news observations in every confirmation quarter. There are zero issuer-quarter coverage failures and zero representation or control TRAIN-support failures.

Coverage volume is still uneven across issuers, as expected from the historical archive. The gate asks whether the intended panel is represented, not whether article counts are uniform.

DECISION D39 - HUMAN-FACING TIMING EXAMPLES

Selection rule
Pairs were selected only by issuer, fold, equal count, and recency-mass spread before revealing future outcomes. The examples do not enter the statistic or gates.

Reading the chart
Fresher news mixes sometimes precede wider future paths and sometimes do not. Equal counts can hide timing differences, but timing alone is not a deterministic volatility forecast.

Boundary
These examples explain the tested mechanism; they do not rescue a challenger that failed its aggregate frozen gates.

DECISION D39 - STOP_N1D_KEEP_EQUAL_COUNT_AND_CLOSE_REPRESENTATION_EXPANSION

Authority
All 15 timing, population, TRAIN-support, control, data, and leakage checks pass. The untouched confirmation contains 8,232 observations across all 24 issuers and six quarters.

Decision
Recency passes the integrity and absolute-ordering gates but fails both incremental-improvement gates. Retain equal count as the simpler descriptive uncertainty-context measurement.

Next boundary
Do not try another half-life, sentiment, source weight, embedding, model, policy, exposure, allocation, PnL, or live-facing change on these outcomes. A future news test requires a genuinely new economic hypothesis and fresh uninspected data.
